subject.title: [Telegram] 机器人头像更改后无法同步到 Telegram 客户端

question: Should OpenClaw mutate the public Telegram bot profile photo from Web UI assistant-avatar changes, and if so should that be an explicit action, an opt-in setting, or unsupported?
rationale: This crosses from local/browser OpenClaw identity rendering into external account/profile mutation using a Telegram bot token and uploaded media, so automation should not choose the consent, audit, and source-of-truth boundary.

options.title: Explicit opt-in sync action
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned action or UI control that requires operator intent, uses `setMyProfilePhoto`, reports errors, and includes live Telegram proof.

options.title: Manual Telegram ownership
options.body: Keep Web UI avatars local to OpenClaw and document that Telegram bot profile photos are managed through Telegram/BotFather.

options.title: Automatic bidirectional sync
options.body: Automatically propagate avatar changes both ways, accepting higher surprise, conflict-resolution, and privacy risk.

recommendation.title: Explicit opt-in sync action
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned action or UI control that requires operator intent, uses `setMyProfilePhoto`, reports errors, and includes live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans avatar identity UX and security-sensitive channel behavior, and this owner has the clearest merged history on the OpenClaw avatar identity surface.
